# thokr
✨ sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

[![GitHub Build Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml)

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |
| macOS    | $HOME/Library/Application Support/_project_path_                 | /Users/Colby/Library/Application Support/thokr |
| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

## Roadmap

- [ ] ⚡️ Performance
  - Right now there are known performance issues surrounding the rendering of
    the tui at each tick interval and/or key press. Ideally each render uses the
    prior render as a base and only makes the necessary adjustments (possibly
    using
    [StatefulWidget](https://docs.rs/tui/0.10.0/tui/widgets/trait.StatefulWidget.html)),
    but I haven't been able to figure that out yet.
- [ ] 🔠 Multi-language support
  - I decided not to launch thokr with languages besides english because of some
    odd rendering issues I was experiencing when trying to input characters with
    accents. It's as though I'm not able to properly input the character in [raw
    mode](https://docs.rs/crossterm/0.3.0/crossterm/raw/index.html). I'd love to
    have that figure out before shipping other languages because I personally
    felt the experience was a bit jarring. I'll open an bug report for it with
    more details and replication steps -- would love more eyes on that problem!
- [ ] 🧪 Tests
  - I've only written a small amount of tests at this point. I haven't sat down
    to really think through what tests look like when the output is dependent on

    raw=ast.literal_eval(os.environ['EVENTS'])

    "number_of_secs": "--number-of-secs",
    "number_of_words": "--number-of-words",
}
DEST_TO_METAVAR = {
    "full_sentences": "NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES",
    "supported_language": "SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE",
    "prompt": "PROMPT",
    "number_of_secs": "NUMBER_OF_SECS",
    "number_of_words": "NUMBER_OF_WORDS",
}
SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES = ["english", "english1k", "english10k"]


@dataclass
class Options:
    number_of_words: int = 15
    supported_language: str = "english"
    prompt: Optional[str] = None
    number_of_secs: Optional[int] = None
    full_sentences: Optional[int] = None
    raw_values: Dict[str, str] = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
    present: Dict[str, bool] = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.raw_values is None:
            self.raw_values = {}
        if self.present is None:
            self.present = {}


def eprint_error(msg: str, usage: str = "executable [OPTIONS]", tip_for: Optional[str] = None,
                 possible: bool = False, did_you_mean: Optional[str] = None, no_usage: bool = False) -> None:
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: {msg}\n")
    if possible:
        sys.stderr.write("\t[possible values: english, english1k, english10k]\n")
    if tip_for is not None:
        sys.stderr.write(f"\n\tIf you tried to supply `{tip_for}` as a value rather than a flag, use `-- {tip_for}`\n")
    if did_you_mean:
        sys.stderr.write(f"\n\tDid you mean \"{did_you_mean}\"?\n")
    if not no_usage:
        sys.stderr.write(f"\nUSAGE:\n    {usage}\n")
    sys.stderr.write("\nFor more information try --help\n")


def parse_cli(argv: Sequence[str]) -> Tuple[Optional[Options], int]:
    opts = Options()
    # Values are kept raw during parsing. clap reports unexpected free args before
    # it reports type validation errors in several clustered-short cases.
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if tok == "--":
            # This command has no positional arguments; everything after the
            # terminator is unexpected.
            if i + 1 < len(argv):
                bad = argv[i + 1]
                tip = bad if bad.startswith("-") else None
                eprint_error(f"Found argument '{bad}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context", tip_for=tip)
                return None, 2
            i += 1
            continue
        if tok == "--help":
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            return None, 0
        if tok == "--version":
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION + "\n")
            return None, 0
        if tok.startswith("--"):
            name, eq, value = tok.partition("=")
            if name not in LONG_TO_DEST:
                eprint_error(f"Found argument '{tok}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context", tip_for=tok)
                return None, 2
            dest, metavar = LONG_TO_DEST[name]
            if opts.present.get(dest):
                eprint_error(f"The argument '{name} <{metavar}>' was provided more than once, but cannot be used multiple times")
                return None, 2
            opts.present[dest] = True
            if eq:
                opts.raw_values[dest] = value
                i += 1
                continue
            if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                eprint_error(f"The argument '{name} <{metavar}>' requires a value but none was supplied",
                             possible=(dest == "supported_language"))
                return None, 2
            nxt = argv[i + 1]
            if nxt.startswith("-"):
                # Observed clap behavior: a hyphen-starting token following an
                # option is treated as an unexpected argument, not as a value.
                usage = f"executable {name} <{metavar}>" if dest in ("prompt", "supported_language") else "executable [OPTIONS]"
                eprint_error(f"Found argument '{nxt}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context",
                             usage=usage, tip_for=nxt)
                return None, 2
            opts.raw_values[dest] = nxt
            i += 2
            continue
        if tok.startswith("-") and tok != "-":
            cluster = tok[1:]
            j = 0
            while j < len(cluster):
                ch = cluster[j]
                if ch == "h":
                    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
                    return None, 0
                if ch == "V":
                    sys.stdout.write(VERSION + "\n")
                    return None, 0
                if ch not in SHORT_TO_DEST:
                    bad = "-" + ch
                    eprint_error(f"Found argument '{bad}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context", tip_for=bad)
                    return None, 2
                dest, metavar, long_name = SHORT_TO_DEST[ch]
                if opts.present.get(dest):
                    eprint_error(f"The argument '{long_name} <{metavar}>' was provided more than once, but cannot be used multiple times")
                    return None, 2
                opts.present[dest] = True
                rest = cluster[j + 1:]
                if rest:
                    opts.raw_values[dest] = rest
                    j = len(cluster)
                    break
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    eprint_error(f"The argument '{long_name} <{metavar}>' requires a value but none was supplied",
                                 possible=(dest == "supported_language"))
                    return None, 2
                nxt = argv[i + 1]
                if nxt.startswith("-"):
                    usage = f"executable {long_name} <{metavar}>" if dest in ("prompt", "supported_language") else "executable [OPTIONS]"
                    eprint_error(f"Found argument '{nxt}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context",
                                 usage=usage, tip_for=nxt)
                    return None, 2
                opts.raw_values[dest] = nxt
                i += 1
                j = len(cluster)
                break
            i += 1
            continue
        # No positional arguments are supported.
        eprint_error(f"Found argument '{tok}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context")
        return None, 2

    # Validate and convert values after structural parsing.
    for dest, raw in list(opts.raw_values.items()):
        long_name = DEST_TO_LONG[dest]
        metavar = DEST_TO_METAVAR[dest]
        if dest in ("number_of_words", "number_of_secs", "full_sentences"):
            if not raw.isdigit():
                eprint_error(f"Invalid value \"{raw}\" for '{long_name} <{metavar}>': invalid digit found in string", no_usage=True)
                return None, 2
            val = int(raw)
            setattr(opts, dest, val)
        elif dest == "supported_language":
            if raw not in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES:
                suggestion = "english" if raw.lower() == "english" else None
                eprint_error(f"\"{raw}\" isn't a valid value for '--supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>'",
                             usage="executable --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>",
                             possible=True, did_you_mean=suggestion)
                return None, 2
            opts.supported_language = raw
        elif dest == "prompt":
            opts.prompt = raw
    return opts, 0

def generate_prompt(opts: Options, ignore_custom: bool = False) -> str:
    if opts.prompt is not None and not ignore_custom:
        return opts.prompt
    if opts.full_sentences is not None:
        n = opts.full_sentences
        return " ".join(generate_sentence() for _ in range(n))

    count = max(0, opts.number_of_words)
    return " ".join(random.choice(words) for _ in range(count))


def generate_sentence() -> str:
    # Sentence shapes chosen to resemble the bundled examples: simple English-ish
    # clauses with occasional articles, adjectives, adverbs, and a full stop.
    templates = [
        "The {adj} {noun} {adv} {verb}.",
        "The {adj} {adj2} {noun} {adv} {verb} the {adj3} {noun2}.",
        "{adj_cap} {noun} {adv} {verb} {noun2}.",
        "The {adj} {noun} {verb} {adv} {adv2}.",
    ]
    t = random.choice(templates)
    vals = {
        "adj": random.choice(ADJECTIVES),
        "adj2": random.choice(ADJECTIVES),
        "adj3": random.choice(ADJECTIVES),
        "adj_cap": random.choice(ADJECTIVES).capitalize(),
        "noun": random.choice(NOUNS),
        "noun2": random.choice(NOUNS),
        "verb": random.choice(VERBS),
        "adv": random.choice(ADVERBS),
        "adv2": random.choice(ADVERBS),
    }
    s = t.format(**vals)
    return s[0].upper() + s[1:]


def csi(row: int, col: int) -> str:
    row = max(1, int(row)); col = max(1, int(col))
    return f"\x1b[{row};{col}H"


def center_col(cols: int, width: int) -> int:
    return max(1, math.ceil((cols - width) / 2) + 1)


def term_size() -> Tuple[int, int]:
    sz = shutil.get_terminal_size((80, 24))
    return sz.lines, sz.columns


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int) -> Tuple[List[str], List[Tuple[int, int]]]:
    """Return display lines and a map from prompt char index to line/column.

    The observed UI uses a 5-column side margin and wraps long prompts at about
    terminal_width-10. This wrapper keeps words together where possible and
    assigns a reasonable position to spaces removed at wrap boundaries.
    """
    width = max(1, width)
    if text == "":
        return [""], []
    # Preserve explicit newlines as hard breaks.
    paragraphs = text.split("\n")
    lines: List[str] = []
    char_map: List[Tuple[int, int]] = [(0, 0)] * len(text)
    global_index = 0
    for p_i, para in enumerate(paragraphs):
        pos = 0
        current = ""
        current_indices: List[int] = []
        words: List[Tuple[str, List[int], List[int]]] = []
        # Tokenize into non-space runs plus the spaces before each run.
        i = 0
        pending_spaces = ""
        pending_idx: List[int] = []
        while i < len(para):
            if para[i].isspace():
                pending_spaces += para[i]
                pending_idx.append(global_index + i)
                i += 1
            else:
                start = i
                while i < len(para) and not para[i].isspace():
                    i += 1
                word = para[start:i]
                idxs = list(range(global_index + start, global_index + i))
                words.append((pending_spaces, pending_idx, word, idxs))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                pending_spaces = ""; pending_idx = []
        trailing_spaces = pending_idx

        def flush() -> None:
            nonlocal current, current_indices
            line_no = len(lines)
            lines.append(current)
            for k, idx in enumerate(current_indices):
                if 0 <= idx < len(char_map):
                    char_map[idx] = (line_no, min(k, max(0, len(current) - 1)))
            current = ""; current_indices = []

        for item in words:
            spaces, space_idxs, word, idxs = item  # type: ignore[misc]
            piece = (spaces if current else "") + word
            piece_idxs = (space_idxs if current else []) + idxs
            if not current:
                # Split very long words.
                rest = word; rest_idxs = idxs[:]
                while len(rest) > width:
                    current = rest[:width]
                    current_indices = rest_idxs[:width]
                    flush()
                    rest = rest[width:]
                    rest_idxs = rest_idxs[width:]
                current = rest
                current_indices = rest_idxs
            elif len(current) + len(piece) <= width:
                current += piece
                current_indices += piece_idxs
            else:
                # Spaces that caused the wrap are visually omitted; map them to
                # the end of the previous line so backspace/current remains sane.
                for idx in space_idxs:
                    if 0 <= idx < len(char_map):
                        char_map[idx] = (len(lines), max(0, len(current) - 1))
                flush()
                rest = word; rest_idxs = idxs[:]
                while len(rest) > width:
                    current = rest[:width]
                    current_indices = rest_idxs[:width]
                    flush()
                    rest = rest[width:]
                    rest_idxs = rest_idxs[width:]
                current = rest
                current_indices = rest_idxs
        for idx in trailing_spaces:
            if current:
                current += " "
                current_indices.append(idx)
            else:
                char_map[idx] = (len(lines), 0)
        flush()
        global_index += len(para)
        if p_i < len(paragraphs) - 1:
            # map newline char to end of just-flushed line
            if 0 <= global_index < len(char_map):
                char_map[global_index] = (len(lines) - 1, max(0, len(lines[-1]) - 1))
            global_index += 1
    if not lines:
        lines = [""]
    return lines, char_map


@dataclass
class Layout:
    lines: List[str]
    starts: List[Tuple[int, int]]  # 1-based row,col per line
    char_positions: List[Tuple[int, int]]  # 1-based row,col per original char index


def compute_layout(prompt: str, rows: int, cols: int, has_timer: bool) -> Layout:
    width = max(1, cols - 10)
    # Use wrapped left-margin layout once the prompt exceeds the content width
    # or contains explicit newlines. Otherwise center the single line.
    if "\n" not in prompt and len(prompt) <= width:
        lines = [prompt]
        char_map = [(0, i) for i in range(len(prompt))]
        start_row = rows // 2 + (2 if has_timer else 0)
        starts = [(start_row, center_col(cols, len(prompt)))]
    else:
        lines, char_map = wrap_text(prompt, width)
        if has_timer:
            start_row = rows // 2 + 2
        else:
            start_row = rows // 2 - len(lines) + 1
        starts = [(start_row + i, 6) for i in range(len(lines))]
    positions: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
    for li, off in char_map:
        if not starts:
            positions.append((rows // 2, center_col(cols, 0)))
        else:
            li = max(0, min(li, len(starts) - 1))
            row, col = starts[li]
            positions.append((row, col + off))
    return Layout(lines, starts, positions)


def styled_prompt(prompt: str, typed: List[str], line_index: int, line: str,
                  global_start_indices: List[List[int]]) -> str:
    # Build a style stream for one line. It displays the target prompt glyphs,
    # coloring already typed positions green/red and underlining the current
    # prompt position. This matches the visible behavior of the original.
    out = ["\x1b[1m"]
    for local_i, ch in enumerate(line):
        # Find the original prompt index for this visible char.
        try:
            idx = global_start_indices[line_index][local_i]
        except Exception:
            idx = 10**9
        if idx < len(typed):
            color = "2" if typed[idx] == (prompt[idx] if idx < len(prompt) else "") else "1"
            out.append(f"\x1b[24m\x1b[22m\x1b[38;5;{color}m\x1b[1m{ch}")
        elif idx == len(typed):
            out.append(f"\x1b[39m\x1b[4m\x1b[2m{ch}\x1b[24m")
        else:
            out.append(f"\x1b[39m\x1b[2m{ch}")
    out.append("\x1b[39m\x1b[49m\x1b[0m")
    return "".join(out)


def line_index_maps(prompt: str, layout: Layout) -> List[List[int]]:
    maps: List[List[int]] = [[] for _ in layout.lines]
    # Use char positions to map visible columns to source indices. For omitted
    # wrap spaces, do not overwrite existing glyph mappings.
    for idx, (row, col) in enumerate(layout.char_positions):
        for li, (lr, lc) in enumerate(layout.starts):
            if row == lr:
                off = col - lc
                if off >= 0:
                    while len(maps[li]) <= off:
                        maps[li].append(10**9)
                    if maps[li][off] == 10**9 or (idx < len(prompt) and prompt[idx] != " "):
                        maps[li][off] = idx
                break
    # Fill any missing cells sequentially as a fallback.
    seq = 0
    for li, line in enumerate(layout.lines):
        while len(maps[li]) < len(line):
            maps[li].append(seq); seq += 1
        maps[li] = maps[li][:len(line)]
    return maps


class ThokrTui:
    def __init__(self, opts: Options) -> None:
        self.opts = opts
        self.prompt = generate_prompt(opts)
        self.typed: List[str] = []
        self.state = "running"  # running/result
        self.start_time: Optional[float] = None
        self.end_time: Optional[float] = None
        self.last_event_time: Optional[float] = None
        self.finished_by_timer = False
        self.logged_current = False
        self.last_countdown: Optional[str] = None
        self.last_layout: Optional[Layout] = None
        self.dirty_full = True
        self.old_term = None
        self.fd = sys.stdin.fileno()

    def write(self, s: str) -> None:
        sys.stdout.write(s)
        sys.stdout.flush()

    def run(self) -> int:
        self.old_term = termios.tcgetattr(self.fd)
        try:
            tty.setraw(self.fd)
            self.write("\x1b[?1049h")
            # Empty prompts immediately show the result screen in the observed UI.
            if len(self.prompt) == 0:
                self.finish(time.monotonic(), log=False)
            else:
                self.render()
            while True:
                timeout = 0.05
                now = time.monotonic()
                if self.state == "running" and self.opts.number_of_secs is not None and self.start_time is not None:
                    self.update_countdown(now)
                    if now - self.start_time >= self.opts.number_of_secs + 0.10:
                        self.finish(now)
                        self.render_result()
                r, _, _ = select.select([self.fd], [], [], timeout)
                if not r:
                    continue
                try:
                    data = os.read(self.fd, 64)
                except OSError:
                    break
                if not data:
                    break
                now = time.monotonic()
                if self.handle_bytes(data, now):
                    break
        finally:
            if self.old_term is not None:
                try:
                    termios.tcsetattr(self.fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, self.old_term)
                except Exception:
                    pass
            self.write("\x1b[?1049l\x1b[?25h")
        return 0

    def handle_bytes(self, data: bytes, now: float) -> bool:
        i = 0
        while i < len(data):
            b = data[i]
            # Escape sequences for arrows. A lone Escape exits.
            if b == 0x1B:
                if i + 2 < len(data) and data[i + 1] in (ord('['), ord('O')):
                    code = data[i + 2]
                    if code == ord('D'):
                        self.retry()
                    elif code == ord('C'):
                        self.new_prompt()
                    elif code in (ord('A'), ord('B')):
                        pass
                    i += 3
                    continue
                return True
            if b == 0x03:
                return True
            if self.state == "result":
                ch = chr(b) if b < 128 else ""
                if ch in ("r", "R"):
                    self.retry()
                elif ch in ("n", "N"):
                    self.new_prompt()
                # Escape/Ctrl-C handled above; other keys are ignored.
                i += 1
                continue
            # Running state.
            if b in (0x7F, 0x08):
                if self.typed:
                    self.typed.pop()
                    self.render()
                i += 1
                continue
            if b in (0x0D, 0x0A):
                ch = "\n"
            elif b < 0x20:
                i += 1
                continue
            else:
                # Decode one UTF-8 character if possible. ASCII is enough for the
                # documented prompts but this avoids mangling common input.
                try:
                    if b < 0x80:
                        ch = chr(b); step = 1
                    else:
                        # determine utf-8 width
                        step = 2 if b & 0xE0 == 0xC0 else 3 if b & 0xF0 == 0xE0 else 4
                        ch = data[i:i+step].decode('utf-8')
                        i += step - 1
                except Exception:
                    ch = chr(b); step = 1
            if self.start_time is None:
                self.start_time = now
            self.last_event_time = now
            if len(self.typed) < len(self.prompt):
                self.typed.append(ch)
                if len(self.typed) >= len(self.prompt):
                    self.finish(now)
                    self.render_result()
                else:
                    self.render()
            i += 1
        return False

    def retry(self) -> None:
        self.clear_screen_soft()
        self.typed = []
        self.state = "running"
        self.start_time = None
        self.end_time = None
        self.last_event_time = None
        self.finished_by_timer = False
        self.logged_current = False
        self.last_countdown = None
        if len(self.prompt) == 0:
            self.finish(time.monotonic(), log=False)
            self.render_result()
        else:
            self.render()

    def new_prompt(self) -> None:
        self.clear_screen_soft()
        self.prompt = generate_prompt(self.opts, ignore_custom=True)
        self.typed = []
        self.state = "running"
        self.start_time = None
        self.end_time = None
        self.last_event_time = None
        self.finished_by_timer = False
        self.logged_current = False
        self.last_countdown = None
        if len(self.prompt) == 0:
            self.finish(time.monotonic(), log=False)
            self.render_result()
        else:
            self.render()

    def clear_screen_soft(self) -> None:
        # The original renderer diffs cells; a screen clear is visually equivalent
        # in the alternate buffer and keeps the reimplementation simple.
        self.write("\x1b[2J")

    def update_countdown(self, now: float) -> None:
        if self.opts.number_of_secs is None:
            return
        rows, cols = term_size()
        elapsed = 0.0 if self.start_time is None else now - self.start_time
        remaining = max(0.0, self.opts.number_of_secs - elapsed)
        # Show one decimal, matching initial forms such as 1.0 / 5.0.
        txt = f"{remaining:.1f}"
        if txt == self.last_countdown:
            return
        self.last_countdown = txt
        row = rows // 2
        col = center_col(cols, len(txt))
        self.write(csi(row, col) + "\x1b[1m\x1b[2m" + txt + "\x1b[39m\x1b[49m\x1b[0m\x1b[?25l")

    def render(self) -> None:
        rows, cols = term_size()
        has_timer = self.opts.number_of_secs is not None
        if has_timer and self.start_time is None:
            txt = f"{float(self.opts.number_of_secs):.1f}"
            self.last_countdown = txt
            self.write(csi(rows // 2, center_col(cols, len(txt))) + "\x1b[1m\x1b[2m" + txt)
        layout = compute_layout(self.prompt, rows, cols, has_timer)
        maps = line_index_maps(self.prompt, layout)
        for li, line in enumerate(layout.lines):
            row, col = layout.starts[li]
            self.write(csi(row, col) + styled_prompt(self.prompt, self.typed, li, line, maps))
        self.write("\x1b[?25l")
        self.last_layout = layout

    def finish(self, now: float, log: bool = True) -> None:
        self.state = "result"
        if self.start_time is None:
            self.start_time = now
        self.end_time = now
        if log and len(self.prompt) > 0 and not self.logged_current:
            self.append_log()
            self.logged_current = True

    def elapsed(self) -> float:
        if self.start_time is None or self.end_time is None:
            return 0.0
        return max(0.0, self.end_time - self.start_time)

    def correct_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(1 for i, ch in enumerate(self.typed) if i < len(self.prompt) and ch == self.prompt[i])

    def accuracy(self) -> int:
        if not self.typed:
            return 0
        return int(round(100.0 * self.correct_count() / len(self.typed)))

    def wpm_value(self) -> Tuple[bool, int]:
        chars = len(self.typed)
        elapsed = self.elapsed()
        if chars == 0:
            return False, 0
        # When multiple key events are consumed in one poll the original records
        # a zero elapsed duration and displays infinity.
        if elapsed < 0.001:
            return True, 0
        if self.finished_by_timer:
            denom = max(1, int(math.floor(elapsed)))
        else:
            denom = max(1, int(math.floor(elapsed)) + 1)
        val = int(math.ceil((chars / 5.0) * 60.0 / denom))
        return False, val

    def stats_strings(self) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
        inf, val = self.wpm_value()
        wpm = "inf" if inf else str(val)
        return wpm, str(self.accuracy()), "0.00"

    def render_result(self) -> None:
        rows, cols = term_size()
        if self.last_layout is not None:
            # Clear prompt cells.
            for line, (row, col) in zip(self.last_layout.lines, self.last_layout.starts):
                if line:
                    self.write(csi(row, col) + " " * len(line))
        wpm_s, acc_s, sd_s = self.stats_strings()
        elapsed = self.elapsed()
        # The original chart always has a one-second minimum x-axis label.
        right_label = f"{max(1.0, math.ceil(elapsed)):.2f}"
        max_label = wpm_s
        axis_col = 6 + len(max_label)
        # Top y-axis label and vertical axis.
        self.write(csi(3, 6) + "\x1b[1m" + max_label + "\x1b[22m│wpm")
        # Optionally draw a simple horizontal/diagonal trace for longer tests so
        # the result screen resembles the original Braille canvas.
        if wpm_s not in ("0", "inf") and len(self.typed) >= 5:
            trace = "⠉" * max(0, min(cols - axis_col - 8, 24))
            if trace:
                self.write(csi(4, axis_col + 1) + trace)
        for r in range(4, min(rows, 18)):
            self.write(csi(r, axis_col) + "│")
        self.write(csi(17, 6) + "\x1b[1m0")
        self.write(csi(17, axis_col) + "\x1b[22m│")
        self.write(csi(17, max(1, cols - 11)) + "seconds")
        h_len = max(1, cols - axis_col - 5)
        self.write(csi(18, axis_col) + "└" + "─" * h_len)
        self.write(csi(19, axis_col) + "\x1b[1m1")
        self.write(csi(19, max(1, cols - len(right_label) - 4)) + right_label)
        stats = f"{wpm_s} wpm   {acc_s}% acc   {sd_s} sd"
        self.write(csi(20, center_col(cols, len(stats))) + stats)
        footer = "(r)etry / (n)ew / (esc)ape"
        self.write(csi(22, 6) + "\x1b[22m\x1b[3m" + footer + "\x1b[39m\x1b[49m\x1b[0m\x1b[?25l")

    def append_log(self) -> None:
        base = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
        if not base:
            home = os.path.expanduser("~")
            base = os.path.join(home, ".config")
        path = os.path.join(base, "thokr", "log.csv")
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
            new_file = not os.path.exists(path)
            wpm_s, acc_s, sd_s = self.stats_strings()
            elapsed_s = f"{self.elapsed():.2f}"
            num_words = 0 if self.opts.full_sentences is not None else self.opts.number_of_words
            num_secs = f"{float(self.opts.number_of_secs):.2f}" if self.opts.number_of_secs is not None else ""
            date = time.asctime(time.localtime())
            with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                if new_file:
                    f.write("date,num_words,num_secs,elapsed_secs,wpm,accuracy,std_dev\n")
                f.write(f"{date},{num_words},{num_secs},{elapsed_s},{wpm_s},{acc_s},{sd_s}\n")
        except Exception:
            # Logging failure should not prevent the TUI from completing.
            pass


def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:
    parsed, rc = parse_cli(argv)
    if parsed is None:
        return rc
    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
        eprint_error("stdin must be a tty", usage="thokr [OPTIONS]")
        return 2
    tui = ThokrTui(parsed)
    return tui.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

                # option is treated as an unexpected argument, not as a value.
                usage = f"executable {name} <{metavar}>" if dest in ("prompt", "supported_language") else "executable [OPTIONS]"
                eprint_error(f"Found argument '{nxt}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context",

                    j = len(cluster)

                opts.raw_values[dest] = nxt
                i += 1

        elif dest == "prompt":

                word = para[start:i]
                idxs = list(range(global_index + start, global_index + i))
                words.append((pending_spaces, pending_idx, word, idxs))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                pending_spaces = ""; pending_idx = []
        trailing_spaces = pending_idx

        def flush() -> None:
            nonlocal current, current_indices
            line_no = len(lines)
            lines.append(current)
            for k, idx in enumerate(current_indices):
                if 0 <= idx < len(char_map):
                    char_map[idx] = (line_no, min(k, max(0, len(current) - 1)))
            current = ""; current_indices = []

        for item in words:
            spaces, space_idxs, word, idxs = item  # type: ignore[misc]
            piece = (spaces if current else "") + word
            piece_idxs = (space_idxs if current else []) + idxs
            if not current:
                # Split very long words.
                rest = word; rest_idxs = idxs[:]
                while len(rest) > width:
                    current = rest[:width]
                    current_indices = rest_idxs[:width]
                    flush()
                    rest = rest[width:]
                    rest_idxs = rest_idxs[width:]
                current = rest
                current_indices = rest_idxs
            elif len(current) + len(piece) <= width:
                current += piece
                current_indices += piece_idxs
            else:
                # Spaces that caused the wrap are visually omitted; map them to
                # the end of the previous line so backspace/current remains sane.
                for idx in space_idxs:
                    if 0 <= idx < len(char_map):
                        char_map[idx] = (len(lines), max(0, len(current) - 1))
                flush()
                rest = word; rest_idxs = idxs[:]
                while len(rest) > width:
                    current = rest[:width]
                    current_indices = rest_idxs[:width]
                    flush()
                    rest = rest[width:]
                    rest_idxs = rest_idxs[width:]
                current = rest
                current_indices = rest_idxs
        for idx in trailing_spaces:
            if current:
                current += " "
                current_indices.append(idx)
            else:
                char_map[idx] = (len(lines), 0)
        flush()
        global_index += len(para)
        if p_i < len(paragraphs) - 1:
            # map newline char to end of just-flushed line
            if 0 <= global_index < len(char_map):
                char_map[global_index] = (len(lines) - 1, max(0, len(lines[-1]) - 1))
            global_index += 1
    if not lines:
        lines = [""]
    return lines, char_map


@dataclass
class Layout:
    lines: List[str]
    starts: List[Tuple[int, int]]  # 1-based row,col per line
    char_positions: List[Tuple[int, int]]  # 1-based row,col per original char index


def compute_layout(prompt: str, rows: int, cols: int, has_timer: bool) -> Layout:
    width = max(1, cols - 10)
    # Use wrapped left-margin layout once the prompt exceeds the content width
    # or contains explicit newlines. Otherwise center the single line.
    if "\n" not in prompt and len(prompt) <= width:
        lines = [prompt]
        char_map = [(0, i) for i in range(len(prompt))]
        start_row = rows // 2 + (2 if has_timer else 0)
        starts = [(start_row, center_col(cols, len(prompt)))]
    else:
        lines, char_map = wrap_text(prompt, width)
        if has_timer:
            start_row = rows // 2 + 2
        else:
            start_row = rows // 2 - len(lines) + 1
        starts = [(start_row + i, 6) for i in range(len(lines))]
    positions: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
    for li, off in char_map:
        if not starts:
            positions.append((rows // 2, center_col(cols, 0)))
        else:
            li = max(0, min(li, len(starts) - 1))
            row, col = starts[li]
            positions.append((row, col + off))
    return Layout(lines, starts, positions)


def styled_prompt(prompt: str, typed: List[str], line_index: int, line: str,
                  global_start_indices: List[List[int]]) -> str:
    # Build a style stream for one line. It displays the target prompt glyphs,
    # coloring already typed positions green/red and underlining the current
    # prompt position. This matches the visible behavior of the original.
    out = ["\x1b[1m"]
    for local_i, ch in enumerate(line):
        # Find the original prompt index for this visible char.
        try:
            idx = global_start_indices[line_index][local_i]
        except Exception:
            idx = 10**9
        if idx < len(typed):
            color = "2" if typed[idx] == (prompt[idx] if idx < len(prompt) else "") else "1"
            out.append(f"\x1b[24m\x1b[22m\x1b[38;5;{color}m\x1b[1m{ch}")
        elif idx == len(typed):
            out.append(f"\x1b[39m\x1b[4m\x1b[2m{ch}\x1b[24m")
        else:
            out.append(f"\x1b[39m\x1b[2m{ch}")
    out.append("\x1b[39m\x1b[49m\x1b[0m")
    return "".join(out)


def line_index_maps(prompt: str, layout: Layout) -> List[List[int]]:
    maps: List[List[int]] = [[] for _ in layout.lines]
    # Use char positions to map visible columns to source indices. For omitted
    # wrap spaces, do not overwrite existing glyph mappings.
    for idx, (row, col) in enumerate(layout.char_positions):
        for li, (lr, lc) in enumerate(layout.starts):
            if row == lr:
                off = col - lc
                if off >= 0:
                    while len(maps[li]) <= off:
                        maps[li].append(10**9)
                    if maps[li][off] == 10**9 or (idx < len(prompt) and prompt[idx] != " "):
                        maps[li][off] = idx
                break
    # Fill any missing cells sequentially as a fallback.
    seq = 0
    for li, line in enumerate(layout.lines):
        while len(maps[li]) < len(line):
            maps[li].append(seq); seq += 1
        maps[li] = maps[li][:len(line)]
    return maps


class ThokrTui:
    def __init__(self, opts: Options) -> None:
        self.opts = opts
        self.prompt = generate_prompt(opts)
        self.typed: List[str] = []
        self.state = "running"  # running/result
        self.start_time: Optional[float] = None
        self.end_time: Optional[float] = None
        self.last_event_time: Optional[float] = None
        self.finished_by_timer = False
        self.logged_current = False
        self.last_countdown: Optional[str] = None
        self.last_layout: Optional[Layout] = None
        self.dirty_full = True
        self.old_term = None
        self.fd = sys.stdin.fileno()

    def write(self, s: str) -> None:
        sys.stdout.write(s)
        sys.stdout.flush()

    def run(self) -> int:
        self.old_term = termios.tcgetattr(self.fd)
        try:
            tty.setraw(self.fd)
            self.write("\x1b[?1049h")
            # Empty prompts immediately show the result screen in the observed UI.
            if len(self.prompt) == 0:
                self.finish(time.monotonic(), log=False)
            else:
                self.render()
            while True:
                timeout = 0.05
                now = time.monotonic()
                if self.state == "running" and self.opts.number_of_secs is not None and self.start_time is not None:
                    self.update_countdown(now)
                    if now - self.start_time >= self.opts.number_of_secs + 0.10:
                        self.finish(now)
                        self.render_result()
                r, _, _ = select.select([self.fd], [], [], timeout)
                if not r:
                    continue
                try:
                    data = os.read(self.fd, 64)
                except OSError:
                    break
                if not data:
                    break
                now = time.monotonic()
                if self.handle_bytes(data, now):
                    break
        finally:
            if self.old_term is not None:
                try:
                    termios.tcsetattr(self.fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, self.old_term)
                except Exception:
                    pass
            self.write("\x1b[?1049l\x1b[?25h")
        return 0

    def handle_bytes(self, data: bytes, now: float) -> bool:
        i = 0
        while i < len(data):
            b = data[i]
            # Escape sequences for arrows. A lone Escape exits.
            if b == 0x1B:
                if i + 2 < len(data) and data[i + 1] in (ord('['), ord('O')):
                    code = data[i + 2]
                    if code == ord('D'):
                        self.retry()
                    elif code == ord('C'):
                        self.new_prompt()
                    elif code in (ord('A'), ord('B')):
                        pass
                    i += 3
                    continue
                return True
            if b == 0x03:
                return True
            if self.state == "result":
                ch = chr(b) if b < 128 else ""
                if ch in ("r", "R"):
                    self.retry()
                elif ch in ("n", "N"):
                    self.new_prompt()
                # Escape/Ctrl-C handled above; other keys are ignored.
                i += 1
                continue
            # Running state.
            if b in (0x7F, 0x08):
                if self.typed:
                    self.typed.pop()
                    self.render()
                i += 1
                continue
            if b in (0x0D, 0x0A):
                ch = "\n"
            elif b < 0x20:
                i += 1
                continue
            else:
                # Decode one UTF-8 character if possible. ASCII is enough for the
                # documented prompts but this avoids mangling common input.
                try:
                    if b < 0x80:
                        ch = chr(b); step = 1
                    else:
                        # determine utf-8 width
                        step = 2 if b & 0xE0 == 0xC0 else 3 if b & 0xF0 == 0xE0 else 4
                        ch = data[i:i+step].decode('utf-8')
                        i += step - 1
                except Exception:
                    ch = chr(b); step = 1
            if self.start_time is None:
                self.start_time = now
            self.last_event_time = now
            if len(self.typed) < len(self.prompt):
                self.typed.append(ch)
                if len(self.typed) >= len(self.prompt):
                    self.finish(now)
                    self.render_result()
                else:
                    self.render()
            i += 1
        return False

    def retry(self) -> None:
        self.clear_screen_soft()
        self.typed = []
        self.state = "running"
        self.start_time = None
        self.end_time = None
        self.last_event_time = None
        self.finished_by_timer = False
        self.logged_current = False
        self.last_countdown = None
        if len(self.prompt) == 0:
            self.finish(time.monotonic(), log=False)
            self.render_result()
        else:
            self.render()

    def new_prompt(self) -> None:
        self.clear_screen_soft()
        self.prompt = generate_prompt(self.opts, ignore_custom=True)
        self.typed = []
        self.state = "running"
        self.start_time = None
        self.end_time = None
        self.last_event_time = None
        self.finished_by_timer = False
        self.logged_current = False
        self.last_countdown = None
        if len(self.prompt) == 0:
            self.finish(time.monotonic(), log=False)
            self.render_result()
        else:
            self.render()

    def clear_screen_soft(self) -> None:
        # The original renderer diffs cells; a screen clear is visually equivalent
        # in the alternate buffer and keeps the reimplementation simple.
        self.write("\x1b[2J")

    def update_countdown(self, now: float) -> None:
        if self.opts.number_of_secs is None:
            return
        rows, cols = term_size()
        elapsed = 0.0 if self.start_time is None else now - self.start_time
        remaining = max(0.0, self.opts.number_of_secs - elapsed)
        # Show one decimal, matching initial forms such as 1.0 / 5.0.
        txt = f"{remaining:.1f}"
        if txt == self.last_countdown:
            return
        self.last_countdown = txt
        row = rows // 2
        col = center_col(cols, len(txt))
        self.write(csi(row, col) + "\x1b[1m\x1b[2m" + txt + "\x1b[39m\x1b[49m\x1b[0m\x1b[?25l")

    def render(self) -> None:
        rows, cols = term_size()
        has_timer = self.opts.number_of_secs is not None
        if has_timer and self.start_time is None:
            txt = f"{float(self.opts.number_of_secs):.1f}"
            self.last_countdown = txt
            self.write(csi(rows // 2, center_col(cols, len(txt))) + "\x1b[1m\x1b[2m" + txt)
        layout = compute_layout(self.prompt, rows, cols, has_timer)
        maps = line_index_maps(self.prompt, layout)
        for li, line in enumerate(layout.lines):
            row, col = layout.starts[li]
            self.write(csi(row, col) + styled_prompt(self.prompt, self.typed, li, line, maps))
        self.write("\x1b[?25l")
        self.last_layout = layout

    def finish(self, now: float, log: bool = True) -> None:
        self.state = "result"
        if self.start_time is None:
            self.start_time = now
        self.end_time = now
        if log and len(self.prompt) > 0 and not self.logged_current:
            self.append_log()
            self.logged_current = True

    def elapsed(self) -> float:
        if self.start_time is None or self.end_time is None:
            return 0.0
        return max(0.0, self.end_time - self.start_time)

    def correct_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(1 for i, ch in enumerate(self.typed) if i < len(self.prompt) and ch == self.prompt[i])

    def accuracy(self) -> int:
        if not self.typed:
            return 0
        return int(round(100.0 * self.correct_count() / len(self.typed)))

    def wpm_value(self) -> Tuple[bool, int]:
        chars = len(self.typed)
        elapsed = self.elapsed()
        if chars == 0:
            return False, 0
        # When multiple key events are consumed in one poll the original records
        # a zero elapsed duration and displays infinity.
        if elapsed < 0.001:
            return True, 0
        if self.finished_by_timer:
            denom = max(1, int(math.floor(elapsed)))
        else:
            denom = max(1, int(math.floor(elapsed)) + 1)
        val = int(math.ceil((chars / 5.0) * 60.0 / denom))
        return False, val

    def stats_strings(self) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
        inf, val = self.wpm_value()
        wpm = "inf" if inf else str(val)
        return wpm, str(self.accuracy()), "0.00"

    def render_result(self) -> None:
        rows, cols = term_size()
        if self.last_layout is not None:
            # Clear prompt cells.
            for line, (row, col) in zip(self.last_layout.lines, self.last_layout.starts):
                if line:
                    self.write(csi(row, col) + " " * len(line))
        wpm_s, acc_s, sd_s = self.stats_strings()
        elapsed = self.elapsed()
        # The original chart always has a one-second minimum x-axis label.
        right_label = f"{max(1.0, math.ceil(elapsed)):.2f}"
        max_label = wpm_s
        axis_col = 6 + len(max_label)
        # Top y-axis label and vertical axis.
        self.write(csi(3, 6) + "\x1b[1m" + max_label + "\x1b[22m│wpm")
        # Optionally draw a simple horizontal/diagonal trace for longer tests so
        # the result screen resembles the original Braille canvas.
        if wpm_s not in ("0", "inf") and len(self.typed) >= 5:
            trace = "⠉" * max(0, min(cols - axis_col - 8, 24))
            if trace:
                self.write(csi(4, axis_col + 1) + trace)
        for r in range(4, min(rows, 18)):
            self.write(csi(r, axis_col) + "│")
        self.write(csi(17, 6) + "\x1b[1m0")
        self.write(csi(17, axis_col) + "\x1b[22m│")
        self.write(csi(17, max(1, cols - 11)) + "seconds")
        h_len = max(1, cols - axis_col - 5)
        self.write(csi(18, axis_col) + "└" + "─" * h_len)
        self.write(csi(19, axis_col) + "\x1b[1m1")
        self.write(csi(19, max(1, cols - len(right_label) - 4)) + right_label)
        stats = f"{wpm_s} wpm   {acc_s}% acc   {sd_s} sd"
        self.write(csi(20, center_col(cols, len(stats))) + stats)
        footer = "(r)etry / (n)ew / (esc)ape"
        self.write(csi(22, 6) + "\x1b[22m\x1b[3m" + footer + "\x1b[39m\x1b[49m\x1b[0m\x1b[?25l")

    def append_log(self) -> None:
        base = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
        if not base:
            home = os.path.expanduser("~")
            base = os.path.join(home, ".config")
        path = os.path.join(base, "thokr", "log.csv")
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
            new_file = not os.path.exists(path)
            wpm_s, acc_s, sd_s = self.stats_strings()
            elapsed_s = f"{self.elapsed():.2f}"
            num_words = 0 if self.opts.full_sentences is not None else self.opts.number_of_words
            num_secs = f"{float(self.opts.number_of_secs):.2f}" if self.opts.number_of_secs is not None else ""
            date = time.asctime(time.localtime())
            with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                if new_file:
                    f.write("date,num_words,num_secs,elapsed_secs,wpm,accuracy,std_dev\n")
                f.write(f"{date},{num_words},{num_secs},{elapsed_s},{wpm_s},{acc_s},{sd_s}\n")
        except Exception:
            # Logging failure should not prevent the TUI from completing.
            pass


def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> int:
    parsed, rc = parse_cli(argv)
    if parsed is None:
        return rc
    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
        eprint_error("stdin must be a tty", usage="thokr [OPTIONS]")
        return 2
    tui = ThokrTui(parsed)
    return tui.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
